3. ATTEND THE MEETING IN PERSON

body from taking further action and moving forward on the agenda.

Meeting Schedule

The regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month,
closed session business will usually commence at 5:30 p.m., when scheduled, and general business
session will commence at 6:30 p.m.

Brown Act

  1
 Agendas are drafted to accurately state what the legislative body is being asked to consider. The
legislative body can take action on "all items" listed on the agenda and be in compliance with the open
meeting laws. Under the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the
agenda, or unless certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The governing body may direct
staff to investigate and/or schedule certain matters for consideration at a future meeting.

City's Vision Statement

We envision a thriving, safe and inclusive community where everyone has the opportunity to access
exceptional services, education and support to be resilient and live full, vibrant lives.

Public Communications

Public Comments on agenda items are limited to three (3) minutes. All comments are to be addressed
directly to the Agency Members not to the members of the public.

Emails for public comment received prior to 4:00 pm on the day of the Council Meeting will be
summarized by the City Clerk, not read in its entirety. A copy of the email will be provided to the City
Council and will also be available at the City Clerk's Office for public review. A copy of each email will be
recorded for public record and noted on the official minutes of tonight's meeting.

Call to Order/Roll Call

GENERAL NOTICE TO THE PUBLIC

The City Council adopted new rules relating to the conduct of the public meetings, proceedings, and
business in the City of South Gate on July 12, 2022, (Resolution 2022-38-CC) and go into effect on
August 1, 2022. Resolution #2022-38-CC is available at the City Clerk’s Office.

MEETING SCHEDULE

Regular meetings of the City Council are held on the second and fourth Tuesday of each month, closed
session meetings will commence at 5:30 p.m. unless posted otherwise on its agenda. The regular City
Council meetings will commence at 6:30 p.m. Agendas are available at the following locations: City Clerk
Office, Public Notice Boards at City Hall, and on the City’s web page at https://www.cityofsouthgate.org

The Public can sign up to receive automatic notices of postings of agendas for the City Council or any
other Commission or Board of the City of South Gate. Visit the City webpage and click on the Agenda &
Minutes icon. That will take you the page where an individual can enter their email in the “Email
Updates” box to register.

PUBLIC COMMENT/PARTICIPATION

Any person may request to address a legislative body during a public meeting. The Presiding Officer will
call upon those present in the Council Chambers.

Speakers are limited to three (3) minutes on any item listed on the agenda, including public hearings.
Under Comments from the Audience portion, speakers are also limited to a single three (3) minutes time
limit. Comments from the Audience is initially limited to 45 minutes at each meeting. Any speaker still
wishing to speak, that did not speak, will have an addition Comments from the Audience opportunity after
the last business item is finished. The Presiding Officer may extend the time limit as long as there is no
objection from the City Council as a body.

To ensure that the public is able to participate, the City provides the opportunity to submit their
comments in person, email, mail. Methods of participation may be subject to change during other such
times when a State of Emergency, Health Order or State Executive Order limits in-person participation.

  3
 CURFEW

In absence of a motion duly adopted by majority vote of the City Council, the Presiding Officer may
adjourn the City Council meetings at 10:30 p.m. The Presiding Officer may ask the City Council if any
agenda items listed should be continued or dealt with during the meeting. For those items to be
continued, the City Council can direct the item be placed on the next City Council agenda or the current
meeting may be adjourned to a time certain at which time the meeting shall be reconvened as an
Adjourned Regular Meeting of the City Council and action upon the published agenda continued.

STAFF REPORTS

As a general rule, staff reports. or other written documentation are prepared/organized with respect to
each item of business listed on the agenda. Meeting agendas and staff reports are available at least 72-
hours prior to the scheduled regular City Council meeting and a minimum of 24-hours prior to a Special
City Council meeting. There are times when the City Council receives written material. revised material
after the posting of agendas, these materials are become a public record and will be available for public
view within 72-hours after the meeting in which they were received. Those materials and any other public
document can be inspected in the City Clerk's Office located at 8650 California Avenue, South Gate.

SERVICES TO FACILITATE ACCESS TO PUBLIC MEETINGS

In compliance with the American with Disabilities Act, if you need special assistance to participate in the
City Council Meetings, please contact the Office of the City Clerk. Notification 48 hours prior to the City
Council Meeting will enable the City to make reasonable arrangements to assure accessibility. For
further information, please contact the Office of the City Clerk at (323) 563-9510 or via email at
yglaze@sogate.org.

SUBJECT:  SOUTH  GATE  HOUSING  AUTHORITY  2026-2027  ANNUAL  PUBLIC
HOUSING  AGENCY  PLAN  AND  FIVE-YEAR  PUBLIC  HOUSING  AGENCY  PLAN

PURPOSE:  The  U.S.  Department  of Housing  and Urban  Development  ("HUD")  requires  the
South  Gate  Housing  Authority  ("SGHA")  to prepare  and  submit  an Annual  Public  Housing
Agency  (PHA)  Plan as part of the Five-Year  PHA  Plan.  The Annual  Plan identifies  the PHA's
goals and activities  to be completed  during  the program  year.

RECOMMENDED  ACTIONS:  Following  the  conclusion  of  the  Public  Hearing,  it  is
recommended  that the South  Gate Housing  Authority:
  a.  Approve  the Aru'iual  PHA  Plan for Fiscal  Year 2026/27  pertaining  to the City's  Section  8
  Program  and overall  Housing  Authority  mission;
  b.  Authorize  the Chairperson  to execute  the Certification  by State or Local  Official  of PHA
  Plans, the Civil  Rights  Certification,  and the PHA  Certification  of Compliance  with  the
  PHA  Plan and Related  Regulations,  in a form  acceptable  to the City  Attorney;  and
  c.  Authorize  the Executive  Director,  or designee,  to submit  the PHA  Plans to the U.S.
  Department  of Housing  and Urban  Development.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  There  is no fiscal  impact  to the General  Fund.

NOTICING  REQUIREMENTS:  Advertising  and  notification  of  the  Public  Hearing  were
conducted  in compliance  with  Municipal  Code  Section  11.50.020  (Public  Hearing  Notification)
and published  in the South  Gate Press on February  5, 2026.  A copy  of the draft  PHA  Plan was
made available  on the Community  Development  Department  webpage.

ANALYSIS:  As a condition  of continued  funding  for the Section  8 Program,  HUD  requires  the
preparation  and submission  of an Annual  PHA  Plan.  This  plan  details  the Housing  Authority's
operations,  program  participants,  services,  and any policy  or procedural  changes.  It also informs
HUD,  families,  and the public  ofthe  PHA's  mission,  goals, and objectives  for serving  low-income,
very low-income,  and extremely  low-income  households.

  1

  5
 Staff will continue efforts to increase  the lease-up  rate to 98% and maintain  the Agency's  "High
Performer"  status with HUD.

Each qualified PHA must conduct a public hearing regarding  any changes  to goals, objectives,  and
policies, and must solicit and consider public comments  as well  as input  from  the  Resident
Advisory  Board  (RAB).

Resident  Advisory  Board  Review  and Comments
The RAB met on February  26, 2026, via Zoom to review  the proposed  plan. The Board  is
composed  of current  Housing  Choice  Voucher  (HCV)  participants  interested  in providing
feedback. A meeting  notice was sent to all participants,  and no public  comments  were received.

In addition  to the PHA  Plan, the Housing  Authority  must submit  the following:
* Resident  Advisory  Board  Comments  (none received)
* HUD Form  50077-ST-HCV-HP:  Certification  of Compliance  with  PHA  Plans and Related
  Regulations
a HUD Form  50077-SL:  Certification  of PHA  Plans Consistency  with  the Consolidated  Plan
* HUD  Form  50077-CR:  Civil  Rights  Certification

A copy of the executed  Certification  of Consistency  with  the Consolidated  Plan must also be kept
on file.

BACKGROUND:  In 1998, HUD  implemented  Section  511 of the Quality  Housing  and Work
Responsibility  Act  (QHWRA),  requiring  Housing  Authorities  to prepare  Five-Year  and Annual
Plans.  In  2015, HUD issued PIH Notice  2015-18,  streamlining the Agency  Plan process,
particularly  for "High Performer" agencies, which are exempt from submitting full aru'iual updates
for four years following  adoption  of the Five-Year  Plan.

The SGHA  has earned "High  Performer"  status for the past ten years, most recently  in 2020.  This
status  is based  on  achieving  a score  of  90%  or higher  on  HUD's  Section  8 Management
Assessment  Program  (SEMAP),  which  evaluates  14 performance  indicators.

The Plan outlines  goals and objectives  for 2026-2027.  Staff  will  continue  to pursue  full  use of
Housing  Assistance  Payments  (HAP),  compliance  with  regulations  and policies,  and effective  and
responsible  program  management.

The SGHA  receives  federal  :tunds from  HUD  to administer  671 Housing  Vouchers,  which  include
Housing  Choice  Vouchers,  Emergency  Housing  Vouchers,  and Foster  Youth  to Independence
Vouchers.  The HCV  program  has operated  in the City  of South Gate since the 1970s  and currently
assists approximately  379 families.  The program  provides  a subsidy  of approximately  70% of the
contract rent based on household income. Current subsidy levels range from approximately  $1,760
to $3,600 per month for one- to four-bedroom  units. The projected  annual program  budget is
$6,188,047, which includes approximately  $623,869 in administrative  fees.

SUBJECT:  APPROVAL  OF SOUTH  GATE  HOUSING  AUTHORITY  MEETING  MINUTES

PURPOSE:  To historically  preserve  the events of the South  Gate Housing  Authority  Meetings.

RECOMMENDED  ACTION:  The  South  Gate  Housing  Authority  will  consider  approving  the
Regular  Meeting  Minutes  of November  25, 2025.

FISCAL  IMPACT:  None.

ANALYSIS:  The minutes  are provided  to the South  Gate Housing  Authority  on the Wednesday  prior

to their  regular  business  meeting.  Amendments  should  be provided  to the City  Clerk's  Office  within

24 hours  of a South  Gate Housing  Authority  Meeting  so that verification  of the record  and corrections

are made  accordingly.  A revised  document  will  be provided  to the South  Gate Housing  Authority

prior  to the Meeting.

BACKGROUND:  The minutes  typically  describe  the events  of the meeting  and may include  a list of

attendees,  a statement  of the issues considered  by the participants,  and related  responses  or decisions

for the issues.
